title: Ephemeral SLO shadowing and stable reopen guard
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: During a recent load spike incident we observed repeated circuit reopen flapping in regional slowpaths: reopened circuits briefly allowed traffic then closed again causing oscillations that amplified SLO violations. This PR implements two complementary controls: (1) ephemeral SLO shadowing: a lightweight parallel SLO evaluation path that computes candidate relaxations for ephemeral windows (used only by the routing decision) without changing tenant quotas; (2) stable reopen guard: a reopen-state debounce and stability verification process that requires cross-cohort confirmation before a circuit transitions from closed->open for the same tenant/route. Motivation: reduce reopen oscillation and prevent optimistic reopen attempts from causing cascading KV cache thrash and burst miss penalties. Summary of changes and rationale: - runtimes/slo_manager.go: new ShadowEvaluator interface and ephemeral window aggregator. Shadow evaluations run at request admission and return suggested transient score/priority adjustments when host-level metrics indicate a short-lived surge. These suggestions are advisory to routing and do not persist to tenant state. - runtimes/circuit/reopen_guard.go: implements stable reopen guard with exponential confirmation backoff and cohort cross-checks; introduces ReopenVerifier that queries health snapshots and recent success ratios before permitting open transitions. - controllers/eviction_coordinator.go: uses shadow scores to bias soft-eviction order during high-pressure windows; biases are clipped by config to avoid starvation. - config/defaults.yaml: conservative default thresholds for shadow window size, verification quorum, and maximum transient priority delta. - pkg/telemetry/metrics.go + docs/observability/slo-shadowing.md:新增 metrics and dashboards to surface shadow-derived decisions, verification events, and reopen attempts. - tests/integration/slo_shadowing_test.go: end-to-end scenarios simulating rapid surge then decay, verifying fewer reopen events and improved sustained success ratios. Commits: - a1b3d9e: introduce ShadowEvaluator and wire through admission path - b2c4f0a: add ReopenVerifier and cohort confirmation logic - c3d5e10: integrate shadow bias into eviction coordinator - d4e6f2b: add integration tests and docs - e5f7a33: polish telemetry labels and lint fixes Files changed (high level): the PR touches runtime admission and circuit state machines, a controller for eviction ordering, defaults, telemetry and one integration test. No user-facing API changes. Testing and validation: unit tests added for ShadowEvaluator and ReopenVerifier logic (coverage ~82% on modified files). Integration test simulates 10 tenants with varied priority profiles; verified 46% reduction in reopen churn under synthetic spikes and no measurable change in steady-state P50/P95 latencies. Load-tested on perf-canary (small cluster) for 4h with repeated surge patterns; memory and CPU overhead for shadowing measured <3% additional CPU at 99th percentile. Observability: new metrics: slo_shadow.suggestions, reopen_verifier.attempts, reopen_verifier.approvals, reopen_verifier.denials, shadow_bias.evictions. Dashboards and alerting recipe added in docs/observability/slo-shadowing.md Rollout plan: - Phase 1 (canary): enable shadowing + reopen guard in perf-canary and one low-traffic region for 48h (feature gate off by default). - Phase 2: enable for tier=beta customers, monitor metrics and verify no regressions in token cost or latency. - Phase 3: default-on for main regions after 7d stable. Rollback: feature gate to disable both shadowing and reopen guard; controller will resume previous eviction ordering. Risk assessment: medium-low. Shadowing is advisory and cannot modify persisted quota state; reopen guard can delay reopen transitions which might increase short-term request error rates for a few tenants but prevents systemic oscillation. Review conversation (summary): - Lina Chen: requested a stronger test for the cohort quorum failure path; asked to add a chaos scenario where a verifier node is partitioned. Author response: added a test that simulates a verifier timeout and ensures the verifier falls back to conservative denial behavior. - Ethan Wu: asked about telemetry cardinality and label explosion; author reduced per-tenant tag usage and introduced label bucketing. - Marcos Alvarez: requested explicit gating config and default safety caps; author updated config/defaults.yaml and added comments. CI and checks: initial run had a flaky integration test failure in the perf harness; rerun after deterministic timeouts fixed and all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, canary smoke). Merge notes: approved by reviewers on 2026-02-17 after instrumentation changes; CI green. Merged via squash. Release notes: "Reduce regional reopen oscillation by adding ephemeral SLO shadowing advisory path and a stable reopen guard to verify reopen transitions. Improves stability during short surges; tunable via feature gates and config." Linear links: ENG-3128 (design + rollout), SRE-142 (incident follow-up). Related: SUP-889 (customer-reported reopen flapping).

notes: This PR is intended to be conservative: shadowing only influences routing heuristics during ephemeral windows and cannot change persisted tenant quotas.
Feature is behind a runtime feature gate: runtime.features.slo_shadowing = false by default.
Operators should watch reopen_verifier.denials > 0 with accompanying increase in user error rates; denial indicates more conservative posture.
